app_note: Caffeine is a naturally occurring bitter alkaloid in coffee tea cacao and other plants.
risk_note: Stimulant sensitivity varies; dosage matters.

app_note: Theobromine is one of cacao's characteristic methylxanthines.
risk_note: Pet toxicity context matters but is outside normal human food use.

app_note: Chlorogenic acids contribute to coffee chemistry and roasting changes.
risk_note: Do not overstate antioxidant benefits without evidence.

app_note: Limonene gives many citrus peels their bright aroma.
risk_note: Concentrated essential oil exposure differs from food flavor levels.

app_note: Linalool appears in many aromatic herbs and fruits.
risk_note: Allergen labeling rules for fragrances differ from foods.

app_note: Eugenol is a major aroma compound in cloves.
risk_note: Essential oil effects should not be implied from normal spice use.

app_note: Capsaicin activates heat-sensing receptors rather than actually heating the food.
risk_note: Can irritate sensitive skin or stomach in high amounts.

app_note: Piperine gives black pepper much of its pungent bite.
risk_note: Supplement interaction claims need careful evidence.

app_note: Curcumin is a yellow turmeric pigment and color compound.
risk_note: Supplement health claims should not be inferred from spice amounts.

app_note: Allicin forms when garlic cells are crushed and enzymes react.
risk_note: Stability changes with heat and processing.

app_note: Quercetin is a flavonoid found in many plant foods.
risk_note: Health claims need source-backed evidence grading.

app_note: Anthocyanins are plant pigments that shift color with pH.
risk_note: Benefits should be worded as food chemistry unless sourced.

app_note: Lycopene gives tomatoes and watermelon red color.
risk_note: Supplement and disease claims need evidence review.

app_note: Lutein is a yellow carotenoid found in greens and egg yolk.
risk_note: Eye-health claims need careful source grading.

app_note: Zeaxanthin is often discussed with lutein in nutrition contexts.
risk_note: Claims need source review.

app_note: Beta-glucan contributes to the thick texture of oatmeal.
risk_note: Health claims may be allowed only under specific criteria.

app_note: Inulin is a soluble fiber often extracted from chicory root.
risk_note: Can cause gas or bloating for some people.

app_note: Pectic substances help plant cell walls and fruit gels hold structure.
risk_note: Usually represented by pectin in ingredient labels.

app_note: Omega-3 is a family name covering several different fatty acids.
risk_note: ALA EPA and DHA should be tracked separately when possible.

app_note: Oleic acid is the major monounsaturated fat in olive oil.
risk_note: Avoid heart-health claims without sources.

app_note: Lactic acid is produced during many fermentations.
risk_note: Commercial source may be fermentation-based and not necessarily dairy.

app_note: Malic acid gives apples a crisp tartness and is common in sour candies.
risk_note: Acidic foods may irritate sensitive mouths or stomachs.

app_note: Tartaric acid is strongly associated with grapes and wine crystals.
risk_note: Food acid use differs from concentrated chemical handling.

app_note: Succinic acid can contribute sour salty bitter and umami notes depending on context.
risk_note: Needs source review for additive usage.
